 Injury Notes: Williams, Haliburton, Wilson, Barnes, James, Bona, Sorber
 By Dana Gauruder |
 at November 12, 2026 1:55 pm 
 Forward Grant Williams is available to make his season debut for the Hornets on Thursday in Phoenix, the team announced ( via Twitter ).
 “Body feels great,” Williams said. “Mentally feeling good. Ready to rejoin these guys and help them win however I can. It’s tough sitting out. I’ve been doing it for a while the past two years. So, I’m just ready to be back on that floor again and play with all my competitive intensity, heart and care.” 
 Williams, who will be an unrestricted free agent after the season, has been sidelined since September with a right hamstring strain.
 Here’s more injury-related news from around the league:
 Tyrese Haliburton will miss at least five more games, according to Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle ( Twitter link via Tony East of Forbes). Haliburton has been sidelined by a hamstring strain since Oct. 26. When asked about his star guard’s status on Wednesday, Carlisle replied, “He’s progressing. Hamstring is doing better,” and said to check back in 10 days, per East.
 Bulls lottery pick Caleb Wilson suffered a right hand injury during the third quarter of their loss to San Antonio on Wednesday, according to ESPN . Wilson was injured when his hand hit the ball while trying to knock it out of Victor Wembanyama ’s grasp. Wilson was active after being initially listed as questionable to play due to right hip soreness.
 Raptors star forward Scottie Barnes , who hasn’t played since Nov. 4, will be out again on Thursday against the Sixers due to a groin injury, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca tweets . The Sixers will also be shorthanded, as LeBron James will be sidelined due to low back/sciatica management, the Philadelphia Inquirer’s Chris Hine tweets . Meanwhile, Sixers big man Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) will be out at least another week before being reevaluated, ESPN’s Kris Rhim relays ( via Twitter ).
 The injury-riddled Thunder could have big man Thomas Sorber back soon, according to coach Mark Daigneault . Sorber suffered a torn ACL in his right knee in September 2025. “He’s done an incredible job of just working through this ramp-up and his journey back to the floor. … He’s got his head down. And when he’s ready, we’ll get him out there. And I can’t wait to do that because he deserves it,” Daigneault said, per Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman ( Twitter link ).
